sutta: Apparently he is called wanderer 33.1. At Savatthi, then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said, "Master Gotama, what is the cause and reason why these various speculative views arise in the world? The world is eternal or the world is not eternal or the world is finite or the world is infinite or the soul and the body are the same or the soul is one thing the body another or the Tathagata exists after death or the Tathagata does not exist after death or the Tathagata both exist and does not exist after death or the Tathagata neither exists nor does not exist after death." And the Buddha said, "Vaccha, it is because of not knowing body, its origin, its cessation and the way leading to its cessation that those various speculative views arise in the world. This Vaccha is the cause and reason why various speculative views arise in the world. So the Buddha says uh cause of non understanding the body and how the body arises, how it ceases and the way leading to its cessation. So we don't see that the body is It's that it gives us suffering. That it is anatta, not self. So, because of that, most people, we desire and cling to the body. So, when you when you desire and cling to the body, this conceit, the ego, arises. You have this I am. Once you have this I am, then you start thinking about the world and thinking about yourself. Like, after death, where am I going? Is the world Where did the world come from? And all these things. So, you have a lot of views, all because of that ego. The next sutta is the same question that the Vacchagotta asked, and the Buddha answered. Instead of uh Instead of body, here the the Buddha says, "Vaccha, it is because of not knowing feeling, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation, that all those various speculative views arise in the world." This Vaccha is a cause and reason why those various speculative views arise in the world. Similarly, in the third sutta, the Buddha says it's because of not understanding perception, the origin, cessation, and the way leading to the cessation of perception, that's why all the views arise. And the fourth sutta is because of not understanding volition. And the fifth sutta is not because of not understanding consciousness. Now, so you see, the Buddha is saying basically, "We group them together." That means because of not understanding the five aggregates, that we cling to a self. When we cling to a self, then all the various speculative views arise in the world. The mind starts thinking. One thought becomes 10, 10 becomes 100 thoughts, 100 thoughts becomes 1,000 thoughts. Now, we come to the last sutta of this third book, called the Jhana Samyutta. Jana is a state. I would translate it as a state of mental in conditions. State of mental brightness when the mind becomes focused and becomes one-pointed and easy that the mind starts to become brighter. Brighter. The higher the Jana, the higher the more bright the mind becomes. This mind can only become brighter when the mind is totally focused. An ordinary mind is scattered. Our energy goes out to the six sense six senses to seeing, hearing, smelling, taste, touch, and thinking. So, because of that now our mind is scattered. It is not strong. But when it is focused, it comes comes all the energy is concentrated. And then I begin to become brighter. So, the Buddha says that for most people, we are sick mentally sick because our mind is so scattered. Only the Arahat is a saint. We are all tikka suko.
